selected_news.title: Starlink hızı Ukrayna’da yavaşladı: Senatörler soruşturma istedi
selected_news.summary: Ukraine says temporary speed limits to the Starlink internet network disrupted its battlefield missions.
selected_news.source_headline: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions
selected_news.article_text: A bipartisan group of US senators has signed a letter demanding an urgent investigation into reported disruptions to SpaceX's Starlink internet network in Ukraine Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said it unexpectedly restricted how fast drones could fly while maintaining internet connection In the letter, sent on Thursday to the US Department of Defense inspector general, the senators say they have "grave concern" about reports of speed restrictions between 12 and 14 October The White House and Pentagon have not responded to the suggestion the US might have had a role in the alleged slowdown The letter, led by Jeanne Shaheen - a Democrat on the Senate's Foreign Relations Committee - calls for the inspector general to find out whether the restrictions were caused by the US defence department or its contractors It says "restrictions reportedly degraded Ukraine's ability to conduct defensive operations against Russian drone and missile attacks on civilian infrastructure" Starlink, which is owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, restricted speed limits on Tuesday night to 100mph (160km/h), meaning any weapons that travelled faster than that lost connectivity to the network The senators also say they are "deeply concerned" by reports of disruptions or "glitches" affecting intelligence-sharing and threat-warning capabilities relied upon by personnel operating in Ukraine "We are particularly alarmed by incidents in which U.S. diplomatic, military, and security personnel were unable to reach designated bunkers during Russian air raids," the statement says "Given the potentially deadly consequences, these incidents require immediate investigation," the senators add The letter's signatories include Republican Senators Thom Tillis, Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and John Cornyn, alongside Senators Richard Durbin, Jack Reed, Richard Blumenthal and Christopher Coons from the Democrats Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds Why is Starlink internet so important on the battlefield in Ukraine? SpaceX owner Elon Musk has suggested the US government may be behind restrictions On Wednesday Musk wrote on X that "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately [the US president]" Starlink is a civilian service that uses satellites in low Earth orbit to provide internet access, particularly in remote areas. Starshield, which relies on the Starlink network, is designed for government and military use. Both are owned by Musk's SpaceX Ukraine's President Zelensky has accused the US of withdrawing intelligence-sharing to pressure Kyiv into ending attacks against Russian energy sites On Thursday, Zelensky said Ukraine's attacks would continue after Russia had continued striking Ukraine's energy infrastructure during an "energy ceasefire" announced by US President Donald Trump on Sunday Zelensky said he had restricted attacks for three days and would agree to the "energy ceasefire" if Moscow also abided by it. However, he accused Russia of ignoring the proposed deal within hours of it being announced The Kremlin never said it had agreed to the deal and Russia said Kyiv had also tried to hit refineries on Wednesday - which Ukraine denied Zelensky has also criticised the agreement between Russia and the US to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel to the US and global marketplace, struck last week, as the US effectively investing in Russia's war effort That deal was the latest effort by Trump to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of the midterm elections, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war, which has sent fuel costs skyrocketing Watch: What does Starlink have to do with the Ukraine-Russia war?

selected_news.source_headline: Shooter kills three children and one teacher at Oregon elementary school
selected_news.article_text: Two people critical in hospital as officials in Bend say 16-year-old suspect shot dead by bystander Oregon elementary school shooting: what we know so far Schools in Bend, Oregon, will be closed on Friday after a 16-year-old shooter opened fire at an elementary school in the city on Thursday, killing three children and a teacher before he was shot dead by a community member The children killed at Silver Rail elementary school were aged five, eight and 11, officials said A seven-year-old and a 54-year-old were also hospitalized with critical injuries, according to police The gunman, who was a Bend resident, has not been publicly identified and early on Friday the identities of those killed, those wounded and the armed bystander who followed the teen into the school and shot him were not publicly known. Officials said they are still investigating if the perpetrator had ties to the school. He shot his way through a locked gate into the school grounds and through locked doors to gain access to the premises, the authorities said Children and staff who heard gunfire rushed to lock classroom doors and hide The deadly shooting has rocked the city of 100,000 residents located on the Deschutes River, roughly 170 miles south-east of Portland, in central Oregon “Please hold your children, hold your loved ones tight tonight. Let them talk. Let them cry. Let them know we are going to rally and care for one another in this community,” said Steven Cook, the superintendent of Bend-La Pine Schools “We will get through this – but not yet. We must grieve for the loss of our community members.” At 1.02pm, police responded to Silver Rail elementary school after receiving several reports about an active shooter. One 911 caller reported an individual armed with a long gun firing at their car. Police did not specify the firearm’s make Dozens of callers stated the shooter had entered the school, continuing the attack inside The attacker used a pump-action shotgun, according to a law enforcement official briefed on the shooting. The official spoke to The Associated Press on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to publicly discuss the investigation In the aftermath of the tragedy, children were taken by bus to a nearby church serving as a reunification center for families. Parents hugged, kissed and held their kids’ hands as they walked to their cars, with some bringing along favorite stuffed animals or other comfort items from home The school serves kindergarten through fifth grade, roughly ages 5 to 11, and has about 450 students and 40 staff members, officials said Oregon governor Tina Kotek praised the intervention as heroic and extended her thoughts to the bystander. “Your actions carry a heavy emotional burden,” she said on Thursday evening Classes, sports and extracurriculars were canceled Friday for all 32 schools in the Bend-La Pine district The FBI is helping local authorities investigate the shooting, according to the agency’s director Kash Patel The shooting began about an hour before the school day was set to end “A school should be a safe place where children can learn and feel secure,” said Bend mayor Melanie Kebler. “Like so many in our community, I’m struggling to make sense of a loss that feels unimaginable.” Gun control advocate Gabrielle Giffords, ⁠a former congresswoman who survived a mass shooting in 2011, said in a statement she was “heartbroken” by the shooting “This cannot continue to be a reality ​in our country. Leaders at every level must step ​up and act,” Giffords said Thursday’s shooting is the latest event in a grim history of recurring gun violence at schools across the US. According to Everytown For Gun Safety, there have been at least 100 incidents of gunfire on school grounds across the country in 2026, resulting in 33 deaths Oregon has passed several gun safety measures in recent years, including a law that requires gun owners to undergo a criminal background check and safety training before being approved for a firearm permit

editorial_review.reason: Kaynakta Bend, Oregon’da 16‑yaşındaki bir şüpheli Silver Rail ilkokulunda ateş açarak üç çocuğu ve bir öğretmeni öldürmüş ve ardından bir topluluk üyesi (bystander) onu ateşle etkisiz hâle getirmiştir. Paket‑in ilk anlatım kısmı “on alt yaşındaki bir genç ateş açtı ve üç çocuğu bir öğretmeni öldürdü” ifadesi, kaynakta belirtilen yaş (16), eylem (ateş açtı) ve sonuç (üç çocuk ve bir öğretmen öldü) ile bire bir örtüşmektedir. Paket‑in ikinci anlatım kısmı “Toplum bir vatandaş ateş ederek saldırganı etkisiz hale getirdi ve olay sona erdi” ifadesi ise, kaynakta “bir topluluk üyesi (bystander) şüpheliyi ateşle öldürdü” şeklinde verilen eylem ve sonucun (saldırgan etkisiz hâle geldi, olay sona erdi) aynı olduğunu doğrulamaktadır. Başlık ve kanca da olayın ölümle sonuçlandığını (şüphelinin öldürülmesi) yansıtmakta, bu da kaynakta yer alan bilgilerle tutarlıdır. Dolayısıyla paket‑in tüm iddiaları kaynakta açıkça desteklenmektedir.

selected_news.title: Hindistan’da genç çalışanlar artık yapay zekâyla çalışıyor
selected_news.summary: Artificial intelligence is changing the way Indian workplaces operate, raising questions about productivity, skills and entry-level jobs.
selected_news.source_headline: India's young workers have a new colleague: AI
selected_news.article_text: Across India, young workers are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence (AI) to speed up routine tasks, whether researching news stories, translating copy, analyzing business data or sorting legal documents But the technology can get things wrong, and relying on it too heavily carries risks Journalist Farah Kazmi, 28, who works for a news portal in New Delhi, used AI while reporting on rules governing stray animals and feeding them in gated communities. She asked an AI model to find the Supreme Court's latest guidelines, earlier court rulings and recent dog-bite cases "Since it can take quite a lot of time to search Google for specific articles about court rulings, previous judgments or recent dog-bite cases, I asked AI to find them for me," Kazmi told DW It gave her a starting point for relevant articles and cases, which she then read and cross-checked herself To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Kazmi also uses AI to translate English copy into Hindi for the Hindi news team, and Hindi quotes into English. But translations need careful checking, Kazmi said, pointing out that in one case, AI interpreted the name "Suraj" as "sun," changing the sentence's meaning "Before using AI, I mostly relied on Google Translate. It was more literal and did not always understand the context. AI gives a much better and more context-based translation, although it still needs to be checked and corrected," she said AI has not fundamentally changed journalism, which still involves talking to people and reporting from the field, Kazmi said "Ultimately, I see AI as a tool that helps with research and saves time," she said, "but the actual verification and reporting still has to be done by the journalist." Yajatt Misra, 28, business strategy and international markets manager at Kanoria Chemicals and Industries, uses AI to analyze data, summarize large volumes of information, prepare first drafts and structure ideas It also helps him turn financial and business information from different sources into management updates and presentations "Things like summarizing information, preparing first drafts, analyzing data and putting together presentations take less time now," Misra told DW Misra said the challenge was knowing when to trust the output. AI can miss business context or get details wrong, so its numbers, logic and conclusions need checking "There is less need to spend time on repetitive tasks and more focus on analysis, problem-solving and providing useful insights to the business," Misra said To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Rakshanda Deka, a 30-year-old lawyer, uses AI to sort large bundles of client documents chronologically or by theme and produce a first list of important dates. Some systems link information to the original documents so lawyers can check the source AI can also help prepare standard applications and petitions using a lawyer's own format and style "If used sensibly, and without outsourcing the substantive legal thinking, AI is basically like having a sincere fresher or junior colleague," Deka told DW But AI can confidently produce false information — making human checking essential "AI often gives you false information dressed up very confidently as fact," Deka said. "So it is imperative that you double-check everything." Deka is concerned that some young lawyers may use AI as a substitute for their own thinking. "A lot of the youngest lawyers are beginning to use AI as a substitute for themselves," she said The use of AI is widespread among younger Indians, with a survey by Deloitte this year finding that 93% of Gen Z respondents and 95% of millennial respondents used artificial intelligence in their day-to-day work An Emeritus survey found that 82% of respondents aged 15 to 28 used AI tools at least weekly to learn or develop new skills To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Dimple Khubchandani, founder of recruitment firm Synoverge Consultants, told DW that employers increasingly want young professionals who can think critically, solve problems and check AI-generated work rather than simply handle basic research or drafting "AI is not necessarily eliminating entire job categories, but it is creating leaner teams and raising expectations," she said Khubchandani said a marketing agency that once might have hired four junior copywriters could now hire one to use AI for initial drafts, leaving more time to edit, refine the tone and shape strategy "AI is raising the baseline capability expected from employees on day one," she said Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), one of India's largest IT services companies, said in its 2025-26 annual report that it had scaled up its "Human+AI" operating model and was embedding artificial intelligence across services and software development Shrijay Sheth, co-founder of LegalWiz.in, an online legal and compliance service, sees the shift across the economy "AI's impact on job profiles isn't an anticipation," Sheth told DW. "It is a reality now. From basic research to strategy, operations, marketing, design and development, AI is changing how work gets done." In software development, Sheth said, developers are spending less time writing code from scratch and more time monitoring, testing and refining AI-generated output "Business, product and problem-solving ability, coupled with skills around working with AI platforms, is valued over mere technical ability to work with any particular coding language," Sheth said To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The question of what happens to entry-level work is becoming harder to ignore A 2025 report by NITI Aayog, the Indian government's public policy think tank, cites data from the Center of Advanced Study in India suggesting that more than 60% of formal-sector jobs could be susceptible to automation by 2030, particularly in IT and business-process services It also warns of slower hiring for entry-level software engineers and identifies junior quality-assurance and Level 1 support roles as vulnerable The World Bank's October 2026 India Development Update says AI's long-term impact on India's labor market remains uncertain The country could benefit from its technical workforce, IT sector and digital infrastructure, the report says, but stronger workforce skills and wider access to AI capabilities will be needed if the gains are to be broadly shared "The productivity enhancement and job loss are both real," Sheth said Deka believes lawyers will increasingly be distinguished by how rigorously they check AI's work. "I think the differentiation is increasingly coming from the thoroughness of post-AI verification and confirmation," she said Edited by: Srinivas Mazumdaru

editorial_review.reason: PAKET’teki başlık ve kanca “Bend Oregon okulunda beş kişi hayatını kaybetti” ifadesi, kaynaktaki “killing three children and a teacher, before he was shot dead by a community member” cümlesinden çıkarılan toplam ölüm sayısı (üç çocuk + bir öğretmen + saldırgan) ile birebir örtüşür; kaynakta beş ölüm sayısı doğrudan verilmemiş olsa da bu beş kişi (üç çocuk, bir öğretmen, saldırgan) açıkça belirtilmiştir, dolayısıyla iddia kaynakla tutarlıdır. Narration_parts‑1 “Bend Oregon bir ilkokulda on altı yaşındaki genç ateş açtı ve üç çocuk bir öğretmen öldürdü” kısmı, kaynaktaki “A 16‑year‑old shooter opened fire at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon… killing three children and a teacher” ifadesinin tam karşılığıdır; özne (16‑ yaşındaki genç/shooter), eylem (opened fire/ateş açtı), sonuç (killing three children and a teacher/üç çocuk bir öğretmen öldürdü) ve kapsam (Bend, Oregon ilkokulu) aynı şekildedir. Narration_parts‑2 “Saldırgan olayın ardından bir topluluk üyesi tarafından vurularak hayatını kaybetti” kısmı ise kaynaktaki “before he was shot dead by a community member” cümlesiyle birebir eşleşir; özne (saldırgan), eylem (was shot dead/vurularak öldü), aktör (a community member/bir topluluk üyesi) ve sonuç (hayatını kaybetti) aynı şekilde ifade edilmiştir. Tüm bu eşleşmeler, PAKET’teki iddiaların kaynaktaki ifadelerle aynı kişi, eylem, sonuç ve kapsamda olduğunu gösterdiği için iddialar geçerlidir.
